claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons are nanocrystalline and contain a high density of grain boundaries and deposition-induced residual defects.
Grain boundaries and defect-induced local strain fields act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers in these films and nanoribbons.
The high density of grain boundaries and associated internal stresses dominates the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The fine nanocrystalline structure creates a high density of domain-wall pinning sites.
Domain-wall pinning impedes domain-wall motion and produces enhanced magnetic hysteresis.
Domain-wall pinning reduces the reversible magnetocaloric effect.
Moderate post-deposition thermal annealing can slightly coarsen the nanocrystalline microstructure.
Moderate post-deposition thermal annealing can relax local internal strains without causing major phase changes when performed below a phase-transition threshold.
Annealing-induced grain coarsening and strain relaxation reduce the number and effectiveness of domain-wall pinning sites.
Reduced domain-wall pinning permits easier magnetic-domain reorientation under an applied field.
Easier domain reorientation decreases magnetic hysteresis losses.
Easier domain reorientation improves the reversible magnetocaloric response.
Relative to as-deposited samples, annealed samples will exhibit a measurable reduction in magnetic hysteresis under low-field cycling.
Relative to as-deposited samples, annealed samples will exhibit a more reversible magnetocaloric effect under low-field cycling.
The predicted effects apply at fields below 100 Oe and near ambient temperature.
The predicted effects require cycle frequencies at which heat transfer is the limiting factor.
The predicted effects require annealing that avoids phase transformations and excessive grain coarsening.
